![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186054676/assets/dab327861acd345bd810b1e21dbe659627c5877e9f00bc2b77eccce8436658ec.png)

Identify the points that lie on the line $y=x+3.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The plotted points correspond to the $xy$-pairs $A(-3,0)$, $B(-1,4)$ and $C(3,6).$

To check whether a point lies on the line, we substitute the coordinates of the point into the equation and determine whether the resulting statement is true.

- Substituting the point $A(-3,0)$ results in a true statement:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =x+3 \\ (0) & =1(-3)+3 \\ 0 & =0\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point $A$ does lie on the line.

- Substituting the point $B(-1,4)$ results in a false statement:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =x+3 \\ (4) & =1(-1)+3 \\ 4 & =2\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point $B$ does not lie on the line.

- Substituting the point $C(3,6)$ results in true statement:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =x+3 \\ (6) & =1(3)+3 \\ 6 & =6\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point $C$ does lie on the line.

Finally, only points $A$ and $C$ lie on the line.
